evidence: tests/campaign/native_production_kill.py:246 `state = {"transactions": names("transactions"), "staging": names("staging"), "frontier": frontier.read_text(...) if frontier.is_file() else None}`; :362 `rec["new_transactions"] = len(after["new_transactions"])`; :658 `ok = sub.get("code") != ACCEPTED and sub.get("new_transactions") == 0`; :666 `ok = (sub.get("code") == ACCEPTED and after.get("identical") and sub.get("new_transactions") == 1)`; :799 `if it["death"].get("lost_transactions"):`. Contrast books/byte-store-log-initializer.lisp:9 `no transactions/ and no allocation-frontier.json (a format-9 store reads neither)`
fix: Observe the record log instead of transactions/: the committed history through tests/native_log_observation.committed_history (what test_native_crash_model uses), counting records before and after each resubmission. A missing journal/ should be a judge failure, not an empty set.
reviewer: tests/campaign/native_production_kill.py:239-252 store_state reads store/transactions and allocation-frontier.json. host/native/io.lisp:4017 and 4594 plus books/byte-store-log-initializer.lisp:9 say a log store has neither, so new_transactions is always {} and lost_transactions always []. verdict() at :658/:666 then makes every died-absent row fail (it requires new_transactions == 1), and a duplicate appended on resubmit of a present article goes unseen. The lost_transactions check at :799 is dead. The campaign is still cited as evidence at tools/deploy_gate.py:588 and tests/README.md:81.
scenario: On any format-9/10 store, names("transactions") is None and allocation-frontier.json is absent, so new_transactions is always {} and lost_transactions always []. (1) Every POST killed before its commit lands as died-absent, and its resubmission is accepted. new_transactions is still 0, not 1, so the verdict becomes `died-absent-resubmit-failed` and the campaign is red regardless of behaviour. (2) For a killed POST that survived, the check that the resubmission wrote nothing (`new_transactions == 0`) always holds. A resubmission that appended a second record to the log is reported as `died-present-identical`. (3) `transactions lost at death` and store_phase (`untouched`/`frontier-advanced`) never fire. tools/deploy_gate.py:588 and tests/README.md:81 still cite this module as the enumerated-cut evidence.
title: Production-kill campaign measures the old per-file store layout. On a log store its judge either always fails or passes without checking anything
